caption: The drawing depicts a single, large, wooden bell-shaped object placed against a plain light background. The main body of the object is composed of vertical, reddish-brown wooden planks that are tightly bound together with several irregularly wound, yellowish-brown bands, likely made of some kind of fiber or rope. These bindings encircle the object from top to bottom, creating a crisscross pattern. The bottom opening of the object reveals a curved, smooth metallic band lining the interior edge. The upper part is slightly rounded and finished with more tightly coiled bands, with a looped knot at the very top. Near the lower edge, the wooden planks have an uneven, jagged appearance, as if worn or chipped away. The drawing includes a signature in the bottom right corner that reads “EDWARD T. JEWETT.” The background is uncluttered and off-white, providing contrast and focus to the central wooden object.
title: Wooden Bell
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
